institutionName: Institut d'Etudes Politique de Lyon (Sciences Po)

questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Please explain: *
Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer:
Location: The fact that Lyon is so centrally placed in Europe meant that I could travel around easily if I wanted to, while I could realistially expect people from all over Europe to be there. 

Country: I really wanted to go to France because of the language and because of its cultural history

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I thought the trip overall was good, but I still consider all the documentation work and communication between universities to very overcomplicated and a lot more time inefficient than it could have been. After all, I surely can't be the first student from Copenhagen to go to a French University, but it often felt that way.

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I think the registration at Science Po Lyon was really easy. They were obviously interested in getting exchange students, so once they had my credentials they more or less accepted me. When I arrived, which I did a little late (1.sep), I had not signed up for the Start-program, but the administration office was really helpful and understanding so they got me signed up, and I got two weeks of introduction with language course and then I could choose between different courses, and the registration module they had was easy to understand.

questions.question: Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: The most important thing to say about the administration office in Lyon is that they are very helpful, kind and answer quickly.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: The administration office. You can have all the guides and platforms in the world but in the end it is about having the opportunity to get in touch with a human being, and that has always been possibile in Lyon.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: Very succesful.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Don't be afraid to ask.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I thought the overall programme was designed in a good way with a lot of different topics strecthing across academic disciplins. I just don't think the particular teaching was very good.

questions.question: Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: I don't think the level at Sciences Po Lyon was impressive. The courses were rarely structured in a way that made sense or included academic work that endorsed analytic thinking. Some Professors seemed unprepared, did not take the time to make a bibliography, spent way too much time giving personal opinions or anecdotes, and were almost provoked by questions from the class.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer:
It was a lot more tailored to the individual teacher instead of resembling certain minimum standards, which is what we are used to in UCPH. 
In Lyon, some teachers doesn't really care if no one in the class room understands what is going on, and they use academic research or data to support their sessions. It was actually quite striking even from the beginning. If you ask a question in class that is perfectly relevant to the topic of the class, some teachers will make a sarcastic remark to you and then just ignore you instead of approaching whatever question you have in a professional way. 

Also, it was in several occations completely impossible to figure out what the criteria for examination was, whereas in Copenhagen the Professors want to be able to test everyone on the same terms, so they make the examination method very easy to understand and then let the academic abilities count. An example of this is to avoid short 1 hour og 2 hour tests, or presentations.

questions.answer: I am not quite sure what you mean by exchange site.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: No because I was not too good at that either. I think one way to go, is to attend some of their community offers, and not just the exchange communites. So if they have a debat club, maybe try that out even if it is in French.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: The only thing I found challenging was the academic procedures. I surprised to see how big of a difference there were from home. Especially in the demands the institution have for their professors. If the professor do not like you, it is your problem.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: I really enjoyed the extent to which they nurture and embrace their own culture. They like to celebrate cultural happenings, they like to go out to eat, they like to spent a lot of money on art and they take pride in their work even if it's administration or service jobs... and then of course the food and the wine.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
1. Be very patient with all the bureaucracy. If it seems illogical at times, it is completely normal. You will have to do simple things such as fill in boxes or ask for a course description over and over, but it will work out in the end, and other students experience this too. 

2. Make sure you don't fall into the Erasmus-trap. That is, only talking to international students. It is uncomfortable, but you have to actively search for French friends, if you want to get a real sense of their culture. They don't come to you, obviously. 

3. Do a little research on the quarters of the city before you go. They are very different and it is hard to get a sense of it before you are there. So when looking for an apartment, maybe see if you can find something in Croix-Paquet, Croix-Rousse, the old city or Part Dieu. You can easily end up in a quarter far away from the nice places or in a neighboorhood that can seem uncomfortable for some, like Guillotierre.
